report.verdict: A clean quarter on the metrics that matter for a B2B supplier: record Adj. EBITDA of A$5.9m (~$4.1m) at a 23.8% margin on revenue of A$24.7m (~$17.4m), +16.3% YoY in constant currency (+11.8% reported), with opex down 2.4% YoY and the 70% gross-margin / 25% EBITDA-margin long-term goals now one quarter away. But the equity is a merger-arb instrument, not a growth stock: Tabcorp's A$0.24 cash scheme caps the upside, the shares sit ~12% below the offer at A$0.21, and the beat mostly sharpens the question of whether the board recommended a sale at the bottom of the margin curve.

summary: **Record quarter with no consensus to beat.** Q1 FY27 (quarter to 30 Sep 2026) revenue A$24.7m (~$17.4m), +16.3% YoY constant currency and +2.1% QoQ; Adj. EBITDA A$5.9m (~$4.1m), +176.1% CC, a record; margin 23.8%. There is no sell-side consensus for this ASX micro-cap, so the 'beat' is against the company's own trajectory (Q4 FY26: 18.5% margin) and its long-term targets.

**Headline growth is constant-currency; reported growth is lower.** Q1 FY26 as originally reported was A$22.1m revenue / A$2.4m Adj. EBITDA (11.0% margin, 64.7% GM). Restating the PCP at Q1 FY27 average rates (AUD/USD 0.7060, AUD/EUR 0.6134, AUD/GBP 0.5250) cut it to A$21.2m / A$2.1m. On a reported basis revenue grew ~11.8% and Adj. EBITDA ~145%. Still strong, but roughly 450bps of the headline revenue growth rate is FX restatement from a stronger AUD.

**Operating leverage: >100% drop-through.** Incremental revenue of A$3.45m converted into A$3.75m of incremental Adj. EBITDA. Total opex fell to A$11.2m (~$7.9m) from A$11.4m (−2.4%) despite absorbing GT Vegas (ex-LVDC) operating costs that were not in the PCP; overheads −11.4% to A$2.6m, staff costs flat at A$8.5m net of capitalisation.

**Capitalisation flatters the margin.** Capitalised staff costs rose 43% to A$2.03m (~$1.4m), 8.2% of revenue, from A$1.42m. Expensing them would give Adj. EBITDA of ~A$3.9m and a ~15.6% margin (our calculation). The A$0.6m YoY increase in capitalisation alone explains ~16% of the A$3.75m EBITDA improvement.

**Gross margin 69.1% (+520bps YoY, +60bps QoQ).** COGS was flat at A$7.6m on 16% more revenue, so gross profit rose 25.6% to A$17.1m (~$12.0m). Management attributes this to digital revenues carrying high incremental margin plus cloud/cost efficiencies in Global Tote. The 70% long-term goal is effectively reached already (Q4 FY26 was 69.8% ex A$0.3m of prior-quarter COGS).

**No guidance change — long-term goals reaffirmed, no FY27 numbers.** The targets set on 28 Aug 2025 (10%+ annual revenue growth, 70%+ gross margin, 25%+ Adj. EBITDA margin over 3–5 years) are restated unchanged. Q1 delivered 16.3% / 69.1% / 23.8%. The only forward comment is the CEO's FY26-results remark that 1H FY27 should continue to demonstrate the upgraded technology and product suite.

**Division driver: Global Betting Services (digital).** The quarterly report does not split the two reportable segments; growth is attributed to 'expansion of the digital customer base', i.e. Apollo-driven GBS. FY26 context: GBS revenue A$43.3m (~$30.5m), +25.5%; Global Tote A$49.3m (~$34.7m), −2.6% reported / +1.1% CC with churn acknowledged. The mix shift to digital is the margin engine; Tote is ex-growth.

**Event engagement quantified only qualitatively.** Apollo recorded 'record levels of wagering activity' in the quarter and, post quarter-end on 17 Oct 2026, its highest-ever traffic on Caulfield Cup / The Everest Day with performance maintained. No handle, actives or ARPU are disclosed (B2B supplier). The bulk of the Spring Carnival (Cox Plate, Melbourne Cup) falls in Q2 FY27.

**Cash: positive OCF of A$2.8m (~$2.0m) after the annual US$2.0m Monmouth Park minimum guarantee.** Receipts from customers A$25.9m (~$18.2m). OCF compares with −A$1.2m in Q1 FY26 and A$3.2m in Q4 FY26 (which had no MG payment). Unrestricted cash A$16.0m (~$11.3m), +A$0.4m QoQ; total cash A$39.3m (~$27.7m) including A$23.4m (~$16.5m) of restricted customer funds (Global Tote Hub/ADW). Zero borrowings, no facilities.

**Free cash flow is thin once development spend is counted.** Payments for intellectual property A$2.25m plus A$0.21m PP&E (BetLine US betting terminals) leave FCF of ~A$0.4m (~$0.3m, our calculation), excluding the +A$1.24m customer-funds movement booked in investing. 'Consistent free cash flow generation' remains a stated aspiration, not an achievement.

**Tabcorp scheme on track for Q3 FY27 implementation.** SID signed 10 Aug 2026: A$0.24 (~$0.17) cash per share, with an election for up to 25% of total consideration in Tabcorp scrip priced at the higher of A$1.00 or 5-day VWAP; implied EV ~A$267m (~$188m), equity ~A$283m (~$199m) fully diluted; 45.5% premium to the pre-announcement close. Conditions: ACCC clearance, gaming/racing regulatory consents, Independent Expert's report, shareholder and court approvals; A$2.83m reciprocal break fees. Board unanimous; directors hold ~10%. Scheme booklet due late CY26, meeting targeted for Dec 2026.

**The offer looks increasingly light against the new run-rate.** EV A$267m equates to ~11.4x Q1 FY27 annualised Adj. EBITDA (A$23.5m, ~$16.5m; company's own annualisation, seasonality-unadjusted) versus ~19x the LTM Jun-26 EBITDA of A$14.0m at signing. Tabcorp's cited 6.1x multiple includes the full A$30m (~$21m) synergy run-rate. The IER's conclusion is now a live swing factor; the market prices the shares at A$0.21, a ~12.5% discount to the offer.

**LTIP Tranche 2 vests — 41.9m performance rights.** The EBITDA limb was met: six-month EBITDA to 30 Sep 2026 of A$10.4m (A$20.8m run-rate vs A$20.0m hurdle) and 12-month EBITDA of A$17.1m (vs A$15.0m). The six-month figure equals Q4 FY26 + Q1 FY27 Adjusted EBITDA (A$4.5m + A$5.9m), i.e. the test is effectively on the non-IFRS adjusted measure. ~3.7% dilution on ~1.12bn shares; worth ~A$10.1m (~$7.1m) at the offer price. This follows 4.825m FY23 Tranche 3 rights vesting in August (2.5m to Executive Chair Matt Davey).

**Cost transformation: the heavy lifting is done; AI is the next lever.** No new program. FY25 restructuring took FY26 opex to A$49.4m (53.3% of revenue vs 61.7% in FY25); Q1 FY27 annualises at ~A$44.7m. Management is embedding AI tools across engineering, product and operations for productivity. Under Tabcorp ownership, A$30m of run-rate cost synergies by end of Year 2 are targeted, mostly from Tabcorp's side (data centres, corporate applications, legacy-platform replacement).

**Product pipeline.** Parimutuel-powered 'reveal games' (commercial agreements with Bragg Gaming Group and Dreamstreak signed in Q4 FY26) targeted for go-to-market in Q3 FY27 — a new content vertical. BetLine terminals for US on-track/in-venue use are being built. New Apollo customers in FY26 included the CrownBet relaunch (Q3) and Stake.com and Dafabet.com.au (Q4).

**Non-IFRS adjustments are small but will grow.** Add-backs of A$0.5m (deal costs A$0.4m, bad debts A$0.1m, severance A$0.1m) take EBITDA to A$5.4m (~$3.8m), +166%. Scheme-related costs (booklet, IER, advisers) will escalate in Q2/Q3 FY27; they are excluded from Adj. EBITDA but will hit cash.

**Below-the-line is not disclosed quarterly.** The 4C format stops at EBITDA; no net income or EPS. FY26 NLAT was A$(5.2)m (~$(3.7)m) after D&A of A$15.5m and a A$1.5m tax benefit. With D&A running ~A$3.9m/quarter, Q1 FY27 EBITDA of A$5.4m implies the first positive EBIT quarter (~A$1.5m, our unaudited estimate).

**Thesis read-through.** Operationally BetMakers is now a ~24%-margin, net-cash, double-digit-growth racing-technology asset — the turnaround management promised. But with the SID signed, equity value is capped at A$0.24 absent a superior proposal; the quarter raises the bar for the Independent Expert, de-risks Tabcorp's EPS-accretion case, and makes the ~12.5% scheme spread the only trade that matters for holders.
**Share price.** −2.3% to A$0.21 (~$0.15) on 29 Oct 2026 per Stocklight (secondary source); the stock has traded in a A$0.21–0.22 band since the SID. 52-week range A$0.135–0.25.

segments.name: Global Betting Services (Apollo digital platform, fixed odds, content & data)
segments.headline: The growth engine: digital customer expansion delivered essentially all of the quarter's +A$3.5m revenue uplift and the mix-driven gross-margin gain, though the quarterly filing gives no segment split.
narrative: They did not break out segment revenue in the Q1 FY27 report; the 4C format stops at group EBITDA and the two reportable segments (Global Betting Services and Global Tote) are only disclosed at the half-year and full-year. Management's attribution is nonetheless unambiguous: the key driver of the 16.3% constant-currency revenue growth to A$24.7m (~$17.4m) 'continues to be an expansion of the digital customer base', which sits in this segment. The FY26 accounts give the run-rate context — GBS revenue rose 25.5% to A$43.3m (~$30.5m) from A$34.5m, roughly 47% of group, while Global Tote was flat to down — so if GBS sustained a mid-20s growth rate in Q1 it would account for the whole of the ~A$3.5m YoY increase with Tote roughly flat, consistent with the FY26 pattern. We will not be able to verify the split until the H1 FY27 accounts in February 2027. By product, FY26 revenue was 37.1% digital and 14.8% content and data, against 48.1% tote products.

On volumes, they say Apollo recorded record levels of wagering activity during the quarter and, after quarter-end on 17 October 2026, handled its highest-ever traffic on Caulfield Cup / The Everest Day with platform performance maintained throughout. That is the only event quantification offered; as a B2B supplier they disclose no handle, actives, ARPU, net or structural margin, so the operating-leverage claim rests on the P&L rather than on unit economics. The revenue model is described as hybrid/variable and success-based rather than per-seat SaaS, which means platform revenue scales with partner turnover — helpful in a Spring Carnival quarter, and a reminder that Q2 FY27 (Cox Plate, Melbourne Cup) is the seasonal peak. The customer base added the CrownBet relaunch on Apollo in Q3 FY26 (an exclusive five-year deal) and Stake.com and Dafabet.com.au in Q4 FY26, and management says the pipeline of commercial opportunities remains strong. Marketing spend is immaterial — A$38k of advertising in the 4C — because distribution is through partner integrations, not consumer acquisition.

The US leg is visible mainly through cash. The annual Monmouth Park minimum guarantee for New Jersey fixed-odds racing — US$2.0m (A$2.0m), versus A$2.1m a year earlier — was paid in the quarter, so the A$2.8m operating cash inflow is stated after what is effectively a rights cost the company is obliged to fund regardless of NJ handle. GT Vegas (the Las Vegas Dissemination Company, acquired February 2026) added operating costs with no prior-period comparison, and A$0.21m of PP&E went into the new BetLine betting terminals and other on-track and in-venue hardware for the US. None of this is disclosed at a profit level; we cannot see whether the US businesses are yet contributing or consuming EBITDA, and we would treat the NJ fixed-odds economics as unproven until there is handle disclosure.

The margin story is largely this segment's. Gross margin rose 520bps to 69.1% with COGS flat at A$7.6m, and management states that digital revenues continue to deliver incremental gross margin — i.e. the Apollo platform carries near-zero marginal cost per bet, so every dollar of digital growth lands at a very high incremental margin. The offset is that product development for this segment is where capitalisation sits: capitalised staff costs rose 43% to A$2.03m (8.2% of revenue), and the CFO said at the FY26 webinar that the higher capitalisation reflected investment in new products, including emerging gaming and vision technology being readied for international markets. On our arithmetic, the A$0.6m YoY rise in capitalisation is worth about 2.5 points of the 13.8-point margin expansion; the segment's reported leverage is real but somewhat flattered.

The pipeline is the parimutuel-powered reveal games — commercial agreements with Bragg Gaming Group and Dreamstreak were announced with the Q4 FY26 report and go-to-market is now guided to Q3 FY27 — which would be a new, casino-adjacent content vertical for a racing-tote company, plus continued Apollo and Global Tote feature development and AI tooling across engineering. Under the Tabcorp scheme, Apollo is the asset being bought: Tabcorp has said it intends to replace legacy platforms with BetMakers' products and run the group as a global B2B engine. The commercial risk we would flag, and which management does not address, is counterparty concentration in reverse — third-party operators that compete with TAB (the very customers driving this segment's growth) will have to decide whether to keep core trading and pricing on a platform owned by their largest competitor. That is a Year-2 question for Tabcorp, but it bears on how durable the current growth rate is.

segments.name: Global Tote (tote products, Global Tote Hub pool connectivity, ADW operations)
segments.headline: The larger but ex-growth half: FY26 revenue −2.6% reported (+1.1% CC) with churn; its Q1 contribution was cost efficiency and gross-margin support, not top-line growth.
narrative: They gave no Global Tote figures for the quarter. The FY26 accounts show segment revenue of A$49.3m (~$34.7m) versus A$50.6m in FY25 — down 2.6% as reported, up 1.1% in constant currency — with management acknowledging customer churn during the year and FX headwinds. Tote products were 48.1% of FY26 group revenue, so this remains the larger segment by sales but contributed none of the growth; on the FY26 run-rate it is a ~A$12m-a-quarter business growing at low single digits at best. Nothing in the Q1 commentary suggests that changed: every growth reference is to the digital customer base, and 'Global Tote' appears only in the context of feature development and of 'cloud and cost efficiencies' contributing to gross margin.

That cost line is the segment's real contribution this quarter. Group COGS was flat at A$7.6m on 16% higher revenue, and management explicitly credits Global Tote's migration to cloud infrastructure and lower hosting costs as one of the two drivers (with digital mix) of the 520bps gross-margin gain to 69.1%. For a tote-hosting business where cost is largely infrastructure and pool-connectivity, that is a durable structural improvement rather than a one-off, and it is how a flat-revenue segment can still contribute to the march toward the 70% group gross-margin goal.

The segment also explains the balance-sheet optics. Global Tote Hub and ADW operations hold customer funds on deposit, which is why total cash of A$39.3m (~$27.7m) includes A$23.4m (~$16.5m) of restricted cash and why the 4C shows a +A$1.24m 'other investing' inflow that is simply the movement in those customer balances. The CFO noted at the FY26 webinar that the statutory cash-flow statement is distorted by customer-funds movements and that management prefers the 4C operating-cash-flow definition. We agree, and we strip restricted cash out entirely: the relevant liquidity number is unrestricted cash of A$16.0m (~$11.3m), with no debt against it.

Global Tote is also where the currency effect concentrates. The international tote and pool business bills in USD, GBP and EUR, and the restatement of the Q1 FY26 comparative from A$22.1m to A$21.2m at this quarter's average rates (AUD/USD 0.7060, implying roughly 7–8% AUD appreciation year on year) is largely a translation hit on this segment's foreign-currency revenue. In reported terms, therefore, Tote revenue in Q1 FY27 is more likely to have been down than flat; the H1 FY27 accounts will tell. Under the Tabcorp scheme the segment is positioned as the global B2B growth engine — international pool connectivity for Tabcorp's rights and content — but the FY26 track record is of a business that needs new pool partners simply to hold revenue, and churn in the base is the number to watch in February.

highlights.text: Fifth consecutive quarter of Adj. EBITDA margin expansion — 10.0% → 11.8% → 14.7% → 18.5% → 23.8% — with Q1 FY27 Adj. EBITDA of A$5.9m (~$4.1m) a record and the 25% long-term goal one quarter away. Annualised run-rate A$23.5m (~$16.5m) vs FY26 actual A$14.1m.

Gross margin 69.1% (+520bps YoY, +60bps QoQ): COGS flat at A$7.6m on 16% more revenue, driven by digital mix and Global Tote cloud/cost efficiencies. The 70% goal is effectively met (Q4 FY26 was 69.8% ex prior-quarter COGS).

Opex down 2.4% YoY to A$11.2m (~$7.9m) and down 7.7% QoQ, while absorbing GT Vegas operating costs absent from the PCP; overheads −11.4% to A$2.6m. Incremental revenue of A$3.45m converted to A$3.75m of Adj. EBITDA.
Positive operating cash flow of A$2.8m (~$2.0m) after the US$2.0m Monmouth Park minimum guarantee; unrestricted cash +A$0.4m QoQ to A$16.0m (~$11.3m) with zero debt and no facilities.

Apollo delivered record wagering activity in the quarter and its highest-ever traffic on Caulfield Cup / Everest Day (17 Oct) without degradation — a credible operational read-across into the Q2 FY27 Spring Carnival peak and into Tabcorp's platform-replacement thesis.

The quarter re-rates the asset against the scheme: Tabcorp's A$267m EV is ~11.4x Q1 FY27 annualised Adj. EBITDA versus ~19x LTM EBITDA at signing — a stronger hand for holders and the Independent Expert, even if the offer price is fixed.

lowlights.text: The +16.3% headline is constant currency. Against the originally reported Q1 FY26 (A$22.1m revenue, A$2.4m Adj. EBITDA), growth is ~+11.8% and ~+145% respectively; ~450bps of the revenue growth rate is AUD-strength restatement of the comparative.

Capitalised staff costs +43% YoY to A$2.03m (8.2% of revenue). Adj. EBITDA ex-capitalisation would be ~A$3.9m at ~15.6% margin (our calc); A$0.6m of the A$3.75m YoY EBITDA improvement is simply more capitalisation.

No segment disclosure quarterly. Global Tote — ~half of FY26 revenue — was −2.6% reported with churn acknowledged; the group's growth and margin story rests entirely on digital (GBS), whose Q1 contribution we cannot verify until February.

LTIP Tranche 2 (41.9m performance rights, ~A$10.1m at the offer price) vests on an EBITDA test that, by the company's own numbers, equals Q4 FY26 + Q1 FY27 Adjusted EBITDA — a non-IFRS measure with add-backs — eleven weeks after the board recommended a sale at A$0.24. Combined with the 4.8m FY23 T3 rights (2.5m to the Executive Chair) vested in August, insider economics around the scheme deserve scrutiny in the scheme booklet.

Free cash flow is only ~A$0.4m after A$2.25m of capitalised IP and A$0.21m of PP&E; the +A$1.24m 'investing' inflow is customer-funds movement, not cash generation. Consistent FCF remains an aspiration.
Deal costs of A$0.4m were added back; scheme-booklet, IER and adviser costs will rise in Q2/Q3 FY27 and hit cash while staying outside Adj. EBITDA.

The shares closed at A$0.21, ~12.5% below the A$0.24 cash offer, a wide spread for a deal targeted to complete in Q3 FY27 — the market is pricing meaningful ACCC/regulatory or timing risk that management's 'on track' language does not address.

EBITDA margin over three to five years — and the only forward statement is the CEO's FY26-results comment that 1H FY27 should continue to demonstrate the strength of the upgraded technology and product suite. The division driving delivery against those goals is Global Betting Services (Apollo/digital); Global Tote is a cost-efficiency and gross-margin contributor, not a growth driver. The parallel 'guidance' now comes from Tabcorp: A$30m of run-rate cost synergies by the end of Year 2, EPS accretion from Year 2 and double-digit accretion from Year 3, with scheme implementation targeted for Q3 FY27 subject to ACCC clearance, regulatory consents, the Independent Expert, and shareholder and court approvals.

forecast.view: **Our estimates (not company guidance).** Q2 FY27 (Oct–Dec) is the Spring Carnival quarter and Apollo's record 17 Oct traffic suggests volume-linked digital revenue is running hot. Against a Q2 FY26 base of ~A$24.0m (derived: H1 FY26 A$46.1m less Q1 FY26 A$22.1m as reported) we model revenue of **A$26–27m (~$18.3–19.0m), +8–12% reported**, with constant-currency growth a few points higher if the AUD holds above 0.70. With opex held near A$11.5m and gross margin at 69–70%, that implies **Adj. EBITDA of A$6.0–6.5m (~$4.2–4.6m) at a 23–24% margin** — a 25%+ print is possible if capitalisation stays at ~A$2m. H1 FY27 would then be revenue ~A$51m (+10–11%) and Adj. EBITDA ~A$12m versus A$6.0m. For FY27 we pencil **revenue A$102–106m (+10–14%) and Adj. EBITDA A$23–26m (22.5–24.5% margin)**; reveal-games revenue from Q3 is upside we do not include. **Leverage** stays net cash: with OCF of ~A$3–4m a quarter in non-MG quarters against ~A$2.5m of capitalised development and rising scheme costs, unrestricted cash should drift up by ~A$1–2m a quarter to ~A$18–20m by June 2027 — unless the scheme completes first, in which case the balance sheet is Tabcorp's problem. **Swing factors:** AUD strength (reported growth will keep trailing CC), Global Tote churn, NJ fixed-odds economics under the US$2.0m MG, capitalisation policy, and above all ACCC timing. The quarter does not change the equity outcome — A$0.24 absent a superior proposal — but it raises the bar for the Independent Expert and lowers the probability that Tabcorp's bid is the last word if the ACCC process drags into the Spring Carnival print.
watch: ACCC clearance and the scheme booklet / Independent Expert's report (late CY26), scheme meeting (targeted Dec 2026) and Q3 FY27 implementation — the ~12.5% spread is the only equity trade.
Q2 FY27 Appendix 4C (late Jan 2027): Spring Carnival digital volumes, gross margin crossing 70%, Adj. EBITDA margin vs the 25% goal, and opex discipline with GT Vegas fully in the base.
Capitalised staff costs (A$2.03m, 8.2% of revenue) and free cash flow after IP spend — the quality-of-earnings test for the margin story.
H1 FY27 accounts (Feb 2027): first segment split since FY26 — Global Tote revenue and churn vs GBS growth; statutory EBIT/NLAT after ~A$3.9m/qtr D&A.
Reveal-games go-to-market in Q3 FY27 (Bragg Gaming, Dreamstreak) and any early revenue disclosure.
FX: AUD/USD above 0.70 compresses reported growth from USD/GBP/EUR tote and US revenue; watch the CC vs reported gap.
Scheme-related deal costs, LTIP conversion of 41.9m Tranche 2 rights ahead of the record date, and any third-party operator customer response to Tabcorp ownership of Apollo.
